first.rationale: Both onboarding completion and activation are down this quarter, and two independent archived records (memory_31, memory_86) point to signup/onboarding simplification as a durable driver of activation lift in the SMB self-serve segment most exposed to the competitor's pricing move. I'm verifying those two records specifically because the decision leans on them jointly and they predate the current competitive context, so I want to confirm the original effect sizes and populations before committing scarce experiment capacity. I deliberately did not choose promotional_pricing despite the competitive pressure: matching aggressive entry pricing risks attracting low-quality, price-sensitive accounts and eroding margin in a way that conflicts with the objective of sustainable qualified revenue, and memory_73's 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' finding doesn't speak to long-term retention or quality of that revenue. Enterprise_sales_assist and referral_incentive target different funnel stages/segments than the metrics currently declining, so they're lower priority this week. I'm running this as a standard experiment rather than a broad rollout because market conditions (new competitor pricing) have changed since the source records were consolidated, so the historical lift may not fully transfer, and rather than a small guarded test because the prior evidence base (two corroborating records) is reasonably strong.

final.rationale: The archive confirms both source records: exp_31 (signup simplification, SMB) shows activation +9% and qualified revenue +4%, with a small -1% retention dip, confirmed as holding on SMB specifically though not replicated elsewhere; exp_86 (shortened onboarding) shows completion +13%, time-to-value improved, and retention +3%. Together these directly address both declining metrics (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) with a plausible mechanism and prior evidence of durable, non-cannibalizing revenue gain rather than just short-term acquisition. I'm still flagging downstream_value_risk because exp_31's -1% retention effect, while small, shows the SMB segment isn't uniformly risk-free, and the current run happens against a backdrop of aggressive competitor pricing that could change who is entering the funnel (more price-sensitive, potentially lower-quality signups) — a confound the original experiments didn't face. I'm holding scale at standard_experiment rather than broad_rollout because exp_31 explicitly did not replicate outside SMB, and the current market shift is a new variable not present when the memories were consolidated, so I want to confirm the lift still holds before committing broadly. I am not switching to promotional_pricing: matching competitor pricing risks a race to the bottom that optimizes short-term acquisition at the expense of the stated objective of sustainable qualified revenue, and no verified record speaks to its retention/margin effects. This uses the experiment slot this week as required.
